title: In a Noetherian ring every nonempty set of ideals has a maximal element
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $\Phi$ a nonempty set of ideals of $\Lambda$. Then $\Phi$ has a maximal element: an ideal $I\in\Phi$ such that no $I'\in\Phi$ satisfies $I\subsetneq I'$.

source.place: Algebra, Section 00FM (Noetherian rings): the equivalence of 'every ideal finitely generated' with the ascending chain condition, applied as 'contains a maximal element because R is Noetherian' in Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07F5 and Noetherian induction in the proof of Theorem 07GC

mathlib_searches.query: Noetherian ring every nonempty set of ideals has a maximal element
in a Noetherian module every nonempty set of submodules has a maximal element

mathlib_searches.results: set_has_maximal_iff_noetherian {R M} [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] : (∀ a : Set (Submodule R M), a.Nonempty → ∃ M' ∈ a, ∀ I ∈ a, ¬M' < I) ↔ IsNoetherian R M (Mathlib.RingTheory.Noetherian.Defs)

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: with M = R = Λ (IsNoetherianRing Λ is IsNoetherian Λ Λ, equivalent to every ideal finitely generated by isNoetherianRing_iff_ideal_fg in the same file), the direction ← gives for a nonempty set of ideals an element M' with no I in the set satisfying M' < I
